facts.fact: Adwave's guide states that CTV typically sees a video completion rate of 90% or higher because viewers can't skip ads.
facts.quote: CTV typically sees 90%+ VCR because viewers can't skip ads like on YouTube.

facts.fact: Adwave's guide states that a 95% video completion rate on CTV is standard.
facts.quote: A 95% VCR on CTV is standard.

facts.fact: Adwave's guide says brand lift studies typically require a budget of $10,000 or more so there is statistical significance between exposed and control groups.
facts.quote: Brand lift studies require larger budgets (typically $10,000+) because you need statistical significance between exposed and control groups.

facts.fact: Adwave's guide gives an illustrative brand lift example showing a 15% increase in unaided brand awareness, which is not presented as measured data.
facts.quote: 15% increase in unaided brand awareness

facts.fact: Adwave's guide gives an illustrative brand lift example showing a 22% increase in ad recall.
facts.quote: 22% increase in ad recall

facts.fact: Adwave's guide gives an illustrative brand lift example showing an 18% increase in consideration.
facts.quote: 18% increase in consideration

facts.fact: Adwave's guide states that typical CTV-to-website visit rates range from 0.5% to 2% of exposed households.
facts.quote: Typical CTV-to-website visit rates range from 0.5% to 2% of exposed households.

facts.fact: In Adwave's hypothetical coffee shop example, $500 of CTV spend with $2,000 in attributed revenue yields a 4:1 ROAS.
facts.quote: A coffee shop spending $500 on CTV that sees $2,000 in attributed revenue has a 4:1 ROAS.

facts.fact: Adwave's guide gives a real-world example in which a local business might see its Google Ads click-through rate rise 15-20% during a CTV campaign.
facts.quote: might see their Google Ads click-through rate increase by 15-20% during a CTV campaign

facts.fact: Adwave claims that real-time CTV dashboard visibility was previously available only to brands spending six figures.
facts.quote: this level of visibility was previously only available to brands spending six figures.

facts.fact: CTV attribution typically uses 7-day or 14-day windows, under which a conversion is attributed to CTV if the household was exposed within that timeframe.
facts.quote: CTV attribution typically uses 7-day or 14-day windows. This means a conversion is attributed to CTV if the household was exposed within that timeframe.

facts.fact: The page states that for most campaigns a 7-day attribution window strikes the right balance between capturing true impact and avoiding over-attribution.
facts.quote: For most campaigns, a 7-day window strikes the right balance between capturing true impact and avoiding over-attribution.

facts.fact: The page says CTV optimization is slower than search or social, and advertisers typically need a week or more of data before making meaningful adjustments.
facts.quote: You typically need a week or more of data before making meaningful adjustments.

facts.fact: The page says that with budgets under $500, there may not be enough data for statistically significant CTV measurement.
facts.quote: With budgets under $500, you might not have enough data for statistically significant measurement.

facts.fact: According to the page, a video completion rate (VCR) above 90% is standard for CTV, and below 85% might indicate creative issues.
facts.quote: VCR above 90%:** This is standard for CTV. Below 85% might indicate creative issues.

facts.fact: The page treats a VCR below 80% as a red flag indicating a creative or targeting problem.
facts.quote: VCR below 80%:** Something's wrong with your creative or targeting.

facts.fact: The page describes a frequency between 2 and 5 as a healthy range for CTV campaigns.
facts.quote: Frequency between 2-5:** Lower means you're reaching new people; higher means you're reinforcing with existing viewers.

facts.fact: The page flags a frequency above 7 as likely over-saturating the audience.
facts.quote: Frequency above 7:** You're likely over-saturating your audience.

facts.fact: Adwave states that for small business campaigns run through its platform, CPMs should be expected in the $15-35 range.
facts.quote: For small business campaigns through platforms like Adwave, expect CPMs of $15-35.

facts.fact: The page states that CTV completion rates are typically 90% or above, because most ads are non-skippable.
facts.quote: CTV completion rates are typically very high, often 90% or above, because most ads are non-skippable.
